title: Tremors
subtitle: seven films and a television series, in release order
blurb: One cinema release in 1990, six direct-to-video sequels after it, and a thirteen-episode series in between. About 21 hours.
notes: Release order, and the prequel stays where it is.

Tremors 4: The Legend Begins came out fourth and is set in 1889, before everything else here. Wikipedia's franchise article presents one order for these films — its own filmography, by U.S. release date — and no story chronology at all, so moving the prequel to the front would be inventing an order the source does not carry. It stays fourth, and its row says what it is.
One of the seven played in cinemas.

The 1990 film. The six after it went straight to video, which each film's own article states, and every row is marked so you can tell without looking it up. The cinema release is the one with a box-office figure attached; the rest have none.
The series is here, with its episodes.

Thirteen of them on the Sci-Fi Channel between March and August 2003, following on from the third film. It gets its own section because the franchise article gives it its own heading and its own table. Sci-Fi ran the episodes out of the order they were made in, and the rows follow the broadcast order the episode list is written in, each one saying where it was made — the other order is stated, never imposed.

All 20 rows carry one — 21 hours in all. The films take the runtime in each film's own Wikipedia infobox; the episodes take the runtime column of the series article's episode list. That column is the reason the series could join a weighted list at all: an episode with no runtime would have counted as an hour and quietly stolen time from the films, so a row whose runtime could not be read fails the build rather than shipping as a guess.
Kevin Bacon is in the first one and nothing else.

One film out of the seven, and none of the thirteen episodes — the franchise article's cast table gives him a single column. He was going to come back for a Syfy series in 2017 and the network passed on the pilot.
Michael Gross is in all of it.
All seven films and all thirteen episodes — as Burt Gummer in every one except the prequel, where he plays the ancestor. Nobody else in the cast table comes close.

The Syfy pilot shot in 2017 with Kevin Bacon: the network passed on it in 2018 and it never aired, so there is nothing to watch. Nor the series cancelled during the second film's production, nor the video games, nor the eighth film the creators were reported to be discussing in 2025 — it has no title and no date, and an undated announcement is not a row.

Film order and U.S. release dates from the Films table of Wikipedia's Tremors (franchise) article, with each film's runtime, release channel and period setting from that film's own article; episode titles, order and runtimes from the episode list in Wikipedia's Tremors (TV series) article; the cast facts from the franchise article's own principal-cast table.

sections.title: The films
sections.intro: Seven films in the order they came out, which is the only order the franchise's own filmography presents. The first played in cinemas and the six after it went straight to video; every row says which. The fourth is a prequel and stays fourth — it is where the series put it, and the row says where the story sits.

items.note: In cinemas · The original, and the only one with Kevin Bacon in it.
Direct-to-video · The first sequel, six years on.
Direct-to-video · Returns to the town of the first film. The 2003 series picks up from here.
Direct-to-video · A prequel: fourth out, but set in 1889, in the town before it was renamed.
Direct-to-video · Eleven years later, and the first made without the writers who created the series.

sections.title: The 2003 series
sections.intro: One season on the Sci-Fi Channel, thirteen episodes, cancelled after them. It follows on from the third film. The channel aired it out of order, so the rows run in the broadcast order the episode list is given in and each one notes where it was made in the run — the other order is there if you want it, but the list does not pick it for you.
